I am 63 years old and have farmed these fields in Quzhou for over four decades. My father taught me the basics, but I also went to school and have kept up with what the extension agents recommend. I know this land well — the soil is loamy, the groundwater is reliable from my well, and the wheat–maize double-cropping system is what works here on the North China Plain.

This spring, my winter wheat is already in the ground. I sowed it last October, right on schedule. I will not change crops mid-stream. I have 12 mu total, and I am putting all of it into the rotation I trust: winter wheat followed by summer maize. Cotton prices have been too unpredictable the last few years, and vegetables take too much hand labor for a man my age. Wheat and maize give me two harvests a year, and I can manage most of the work with my own small tractor and seeder.

For the wheat, I planted Jimai 22 — an improved variety with good stripe rust resistance. I did rotary tillage before sowing and put down 32 jin of seed per mu. Now that the wheat is greening up, I will topdress with urea and run the border irrigation twice more before harvest in early June. I expect about 1,100 jin per mu if the weather cooperates.

For maize, I will switch to no-tillage planting right after the wheat comes off. I have seen too many neighbors lose a week plowing and then get caught by early dry spells. Denghai 605 is the hybrid I will use — it has done well here for years. I will plant 1.2 packages per mu and apply my basal compound fertilizer at sowing. Two irrigations will be enough for maize if I time them around tasseling and grain-filling. I expect around 1,150 jin per mu.

I keep my pesticide use moderate. On wheat, I will spray four times: herbicide once, fungicide once, and insecticide twice for aphids and armyworm. On maize, three applications will do — herbicide at early stage, insecticide twice for bollworm and corn borer.

Because I have some schooling, I pay attention to not over-fertilizing. I will use about 70 kg of nitrogen per mu on the wheat and 25 kg on the maize. Phosphorus and potassium come mostly from the compound fertilizer I apply at basal — around 18 kg P₂O₅ and 5 kg K₂O for wheat, and about 7 kg each for maize. That is enough for this soil.
